    Evidence
    The landing’s three numbers, unpacked. Counts are from the runs in TESTING.md. Device: no. Meta key: no.

    
      The three numbers
      
        5 piecesThe synthetic room yadori_den reports five labelled meshes: couch, lamp, plant, screen, table.
        0 keysThe browser never sees MODEL_API_KEY. Only the gateway reads it, and the contract tests assert it is never echoed.
        1 pinchOne hand pinch wakes the couch. The face centre sat on the computed target at 0.00 cm (limit 1 cm).
      
      Also measured Oct 25: XR CPU p50 0.70 ms, p95 1.00 ms, 26 draw calls; 82 unit tests; emulator 21/21; glasses profile 8/8; browser diorama 18/18; responsive 12/12. Quest frame time is unverified. Full table: TESTING.md.
    

    
      How a wake works
      
        Point and pinch. Quest Space Setup (or the emulator room) already holds furniture-sized boxes. A hand ray draws a dotted outline and a label chip. Pinch, or click in the browser.
        A face blooms. On the side that faces you, in its upper third, 1 cm proud of the surface, held by a WebXR anchor. It blinks, follows you, and turns at most 40° toward you.
        Poke, pet, flick. A fingertip poke makes it jump. A slow palm stroke makes it purr. A flick sends it spinning and grumpy. In the browser: tap, rub, swipe.
        Wake a second. With a key, Muse Spark writes a persona from the label and the neighbours, and ask_object lets them gossip (at most two hops). Without a key you type both lines. Puppet mode, labelled.
      
    

    
      The binder
      Each woken object is a card. Six spirits at most, because a site gets eight persistent anchors. These two pockets are from a recorded IWER run, not from a real home.
      
        Couch · 2.0 × 0.9 m
        Lamp · 0.4 × 1.7 m
      
    

    
      What runs, and what waits
      
        Pick the objectWith the key. Pinch a labelled mesh.Right now. The same pinch, or a click.
        FaceWith the key. Muse Image sheet, 10 images, about $0.10.Right now. Built-in face, labelled “not generated”.
        Personality and repliesWith the key. Muse Spark, six tools.Right now. Puppet mode. You type the lines.
        Voice inWith the key. Muse Voice Transcribe.Right now. Typing.
        Voice outWith the weights. Meta MMS-TTS, open weights, CC-BY-NC-4.0.Right now. After fetch-models.sh, or the browser voice, labelled.
        Anchors, gestures, gaze, gossipEither way. Local. The same code.Right now. Identical. No network model.
      
      Never a canned reply. Without the key, chat, transcribe and cut return 503 setup_required.
      Not built: phone clip capture, tracking and export; the camera probe and crop picker; SAM sheet-part cutting; and realtime voice streaming. Phones run the browser diorama. Voice input uses a WAV upload when the key is configured; live Meta calls and headset frame time remain unverified.
    

    
      How to open it
      
        No headset. pnpm gateway, then pnpm --filter app dev, then open https://localhost:8091/. The room is labelled “Browser diorama, not your room”. Click a piece of furniture.
        Desktop emulator. On that same page, “Enter mixed reality (emulated)” uses IWER’s synthetic room. Hands only.
        Quest 3 / 3S. Run Space Setup so the furniture is labelled, open the app in the Quest browser, enter mixed reality, point and pinch. Not run on a headset yet. Steps: docs/QUEST.md.
      
    

    
      Questions
      Can it wake a mug?Not in the headset. The room model holds furniture-sized boxes from Space Setup. Small things need camera access, which Quest Browser does not reliably give a web app yet.
      Where does my voice go?To the Yadori gateway, which sends it to Muse Voice Transcribe. No audio is stored. The spirits’ voices are made on the gateway.
      Does the face stick to the couch?It is placed on the couch’s detected box and fixed with a WebXR anchor. In the emulator the face centre sat on the computed target within 1 cm (measured 0.00 cm).
      Is the key ever in the browser?No. Only the gateway reads MODEL_API_KEY. The app talks to /api.
